chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the stillness of the sun, and he said:
"O Muhammad, how small is your frame and how difficult is your question; and indeed, you are worthy of an answer.

When the sun rises, seventy thousand angels draw it, after five thousand angels from among the angels have taken hold of each of its rays, between one pulling and one pushing, until when it reaches the atmosphere and passes the opening, the angel of light turns it from back to front, so what had been facing the earth turns toward the heaven, and its rays reach the boundaries of the Throne. At that moment the angels call out: "Glory be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and
"All praise is due to Allah, Who has not taken a consort, nor a son, and He has no partner in the dominion, nor does He have any protector out of weakness; and magnify Him with great magnification."

He said to him, "May I be your ransom, should I preserve this speech at the sun's decline?" He said, "Yes, preserve it as you preserve your eye; for when the sun declines, the angels are behind it glorifying Allah in the orbit of the atmosphere until it sets.

key_terms.الشَّمْسِ: the sun, whose motion is described in the narration
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, whose boundaries the sun's rays reach
key_terms.الْمُلْكِ: dominion or sovereignty, negating any partner with Allah in His rule
key_terms.رُكُودِ: the stillness or pause of the sun being asked about
key_terms.زَوَالِ: the sun's decline from the meridian, a devotional time mentioned here
key_terms.شُعَاعٍ: a ray of the sun attended by angels
key_terms.مَلَكٍ: an angel involved in drawing or directing the sun
key_terms.يُسَبِّحُونَ: they glorify Allah, describing the angels' act of tasbih

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the sun's movement and the remembrance to recite at zawal?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a cosmological account of the sun's movement and the role of the angels in relation to it. It also teaches a form of dhikr and praise of Allah at the time of the sun's decline, emphasizing tawhid and divine transcendence.
